notes:
Lead source: self-serve signup. Primary contact: Ana Vargas (CTO).
Problem statement: customer-facing chat is showing variable latency after moving traffic closer to EU. P95 observed ~800-1200ms in EU tests, P50 ~200-300ms. End users report delayed typing/hand-off; visible UX regressions.
Workload: chat-first (support workflows), occasional doc-search, server-side summarization of product pages. Typical prompt payloads are heavy — they include ~800-1,200 tokens of product/context + user message. Many requests set max_tokens=512 by default.
Environment: Hosted API preferred (public cloud). They are cost-sensitive (SMB), running on trial credits. No Dedicated/Private interest at this stage.
Security: light requirements — need audit logging and basic retention controls; SOC2 is roadmap but not currently blocking.
What we saw / replicated: SE ran synthetic requests from eu-west-1 and us-east-1. EU P95 spikes correlated with larger prompt sizes and occasional CPU contention on shared infra during their peak (10:30-12:30 CET). NA region (us-east-1) consistently ~150-300ms P95.
Immediate recommendations provided during call:
  - Region: route critical chat traffic to us-east-1 or us-west-2 for lower observed P95; keep EU for EU-only users pending deeper investigation.
  - Timeouts: set client-side request timeout header to 30s (avoid default very low timeouts); set server retry/backoff for idempotent calls.
  - Prompt length: reduce context where possible, truncate product catalog to top 5 bullets, move long context to embeddings/doc-search path and call embedding+retrieval (reduces token size). Aim for ~200-400 token user+context for chat quick responses.
  - Token limits: lower max_tokens to 256 for routine assistant reply; use generate/streaming for long responses to improve perceived latency.
  - Model variant: suggest redwood-1-medium for chat; redwood-1-small for purely technical linting/QA tasks.
  - Streaming: enable streaming=true for UI to render partial tokens and improve UX during spikes.
  - Caching: implement simple prefix caching on repeated product queries (we sent code snippet), consider KV caching for frequent user-session context.
Follow-ups and ownership: AE (Maya) to send perf tuning doc and a short checklist by 2026-03-11 (pricing and quick fixes). SE (Ravi) to run cross-region test with ephemeral NA key on 2026-03-12 and attach CSV results to drive.
